title: kbid.py add titles a raw source code file by its first comment line, which can hold an author email address
goal: a source row kbid.py add writes for a raw source code file (a text/plain page such as a raw.githubusercontent.com file) never takes its title from a comment line of the file: the title names the repository path, or add refuses and asks for --title

run:
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '_tools'); import provider
t = '#
# Author:: Jan Kowalski (<' + 'jan.kowalski' + '@corp.example.com>)
# License:: Apache License, Version 2.0

class Chef
end
'
title = provider._page_head(t, 'text/plain; charset=utf-8')[0]
print('title read from a plain-text code file:', repr(title))
sys.exit(1 if '@' in title or title.startswith('Author::') else 0)

gates.question: How does kbid.py add title a raw plain-text file that is not Markdown: the repository path, or refuse and ask for --title? (Markdown is told by a .md, .markdown or .mdx path)

notes: Found 2026-10-21 landing ST-polh634k: rows S-u5nsu5mz and S-uajt3oqr were titled 'Author:: <name> (<email>)' from the chef/chef file headers, and test_leaks failed the sync gate on the two email addresses; the worker also recorded MIT while the files state Apache-2.0 (provider.read_licence got 403 from the GitHub REST API, unauthenticated limit). Fixed by hand in 28d31c7590. Premise: provider._page_head on a planted text/plain header returns the Author:: line as the title; the repro exits 1.
